draft.title: Elevation / shadow rgba + z-index scale grounding
draft.principle_summary: Shadow-stack progression (blur widening, alpha climbing per elevation step) has a real physical direction, not just an aesthetic guess: for a fixed light source, a cast shadow's soft edge (penumbra) widens as the object lifts further from the surface it shadows, and Google's own Material Design shadow system (a named, citable convention, not an empirical study) formalizes that same widen-blur/shift-opacity pattern into layered key + ambient shadows. Z-index tier spacing has a separate, equally nameable grounding: sparse enumeration, the standard software convention (documented explicitly in Bootstrap's own z-index scale) of leaving numeric gaps between semantically distinct layers so a later insertion never forces a renumber, while pairs that will never have anything inserted between them (a scrim and its own sheet/modal) get a tight gap instead.

sources.claim: Material Design's elevation shadow system layers a key shadow (directional, tighter) over an ambient shadow (diffuse, wider), with named opacity constants (key-umbra 0.20, key-penumbra 0.14, ambient 0.12) that shift as elevation (dp) increases: blur and offset grow, opacity per layer changes together.

The soft edge (penumbra) of a cast shadow widens as the distance between the object and the surface it is shadowing increases, for a light source of fixed size: this is a general fact of shadow-formation optics, not a specific study result.
sources.source: General geometric-optics shadow formation (umbra/penumbra/antumbra); overview at Wikipedia 'Umbra, penumbra and antumbra'

sources.claim: Sparse enumeration, using deliberate numeric gaps (e.g. increments of 10 or 100) rather than consecutive integers in a z-index or line-numbering scale, is a named, widely used engineering convention for leaving room to insert new layers/lines later without renumbering everything.
sources.source: Bootstrap z-index utility docs, getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/utilities/z-index (documents Bootstrap's own 1000/1010/1020...1070 gapped scale explicitly for this reason)

draft.solen_current: RATIONALE.md section 14 ("### Box shadow elevation value table", lines 400-406) already states the DECISION/FORCES/OPTIMIZES-FOR for elevation-1/2/3/pressed and grounds "why a shadow exists at all" in Gestalt figure/ground (T1), but its MECHANIC line (405) and SACRIFICES line (404) explicitly say the specific rgba/blur/spread numbers are "CONV, not a measured value" with "no formula to extend from." Section 14's z-index entry (lines 408-414) is the same shape: figure/ground grounds that SOME stacking order should exist (T1), but the SACRIFICES line (412) flags the 100-point tier gaps as "generous headroom that is never explained." Domain 14 (section 18, lines 717-726, "depth, light, and materiality") separately already grounds the shadow DIRECTION and general two-layer STRUCTURE: light-from-above prior (T2, Ramachandran 1988) for why shadows go down/pressed goes inset, and the two-light (key+ambient) model (CONV, Material's elevation system) for why the token is a two-layer stack at all (line 721 explicitly calls this "the mechanic for the section-14 shadow block, upgrading it from bare CONV"). LOCKFILE:481-486 holds the frozen literal rgba/blur/spread numbers; LOCKFILE:494-497 holds the frozen z-index numbers.
draft.gap: Two specific things are still bare inside an otherwise well-grounded section: (1) the PROGRESSION itself, why blur triples (3px to 12px to 28px) and alpha roughly doubles (.04/.03 to .08/.04 to .12/.06) per elevation step, rather than climbing linearly or by any other shape, and why that progression should logically continue if a future elevation-4 is ever added; (2) the UNEQUAL z-index gap sizes, why sheet-bg to sheet and modal-bg to modal are only 10 apart while sheet to modal-bg is 90 and toast to tooltip is 100, which the file currently flags as unexplained rather than naming the recognized convention it already matches. Both are gaps of missing CITATION, not missing literals: no frozen value changes.
draft.proposed_addition:
Two new paragraphs for RATIONALE.md section 18 (Domain 14: depth, light, and materiality), inserted after the existing two-light-model paragraph (after line 721), grounding LOCKFILE:481-486 and LOCKFILE:494-497 without touching any frozen value:

### Shadow blur and alpha progression (extends LOCKFILE:481-486, section-14 box shadow table)
DECISION: unchanged, the LOCKFILE elevation-1 through elevation-3 plus pressed two-layer rgba stacks (blur 3px to 12px to 28px, key-layer alpha .04 to .08 to .12, second-layer alpha .03 to .04 to .06).
FORCES: a higher elevation needs to read as MORE lifted without the top of the ladder looking pasted on or overly dark; the step sizes need to keep growing (not stay linear) or level 3 would look like level 2 with a filter on it.
OPTIMIZES FOR: a three-step ladder where each step is unambiguously more lifted than the last, judged by eye against a real-world reference rather than an arbitrary curve.
SACRIFICES: the exact multiplier between steps (roughly 4x blur from level 1 to level 2, then a smaller relative jump to level 3) is still tuned by eye, not derived from a formula; this addition narrows the "no formula to extend from" gap but does not close it.
BOUNDARY: this grounds DIRECTION (blur should widen, alpha should climb, together, as elevation increases) and PRECEDENT (a named system already does this), not the exact Solen numbers, which stay CONV.
MECHANIC: two facts, one physical and one conventional, both already point the same direction section 18's two-light-model paragraph names. Physically (T1, general shadow-formation optics), for a fixed-size light source, the penumbra (the shadow's soft edge) widens as the distance between the object and the surface it shadows grows, so an element sitting further above its surface casting a wider, softer shadow is physically correct, not an arbitrary aesthetic choice. Conventionally (CONV), Google's own Material Design shadow system formalizes the identical pattern into a named, citable elevation scale: a key shadow (tighter, higher opacity) layered under an ambient shadow (wider, lower opacity), both shifting together as dp/elevation increases. Solen's two-layer stack is the same two-shadow shape at three steps instead of Material's 25 (0-24dp); the numbers differ (Material's constants are fixed opacities of 0.20/0.14/0.12 per layer type, Solen's climb per elevation step instead), so this is precedent for the SHAPE of the progression, not a source for the specific rgba values, which remain owner-tuned CONV.
SOURCE: Material Design shadows resource (CONV), m1.material.io/resources/shadows.html; general umbra/penumbra shadow-formation optics (T1); LOCKFILE:481-486; RATIONALE.md section 18 (light-from-above, two-light model, already present).

### Z-index tier gap sizing (extends LOCKFILE:494-497, section-14 z-index scale)
DECISION: unchanged, sheet-bg 400 / sheet 410 / modal-bg 500 / modal 510 / toast 600 / tooltip 700, with header/tab-nav and sticky-rail on a separate small-number scale (z-50, z-30).
FORCES: overlays need an unambiguous stacking order regardless of DOM mount order; a future overlay type needs to be insertable without renumbering the whole scale; a background/scrim and its own foreground content never need anything inserted between them, so they don't need the same headroom as two unrelated overlay types.
OPTIMIZES FOR: an extensible scale where inserting a new layer type is a matter of picking a free number in an existing gap, never a renumbering exercise.
SACRIFICES: same as before, this names why the gaps exist and why they are unequal, it does not derive the exact gap sizes (10 versus 90 versus 100) from a formula.
BOUNDARY: this grounds the PATTERN (gapped, unequal spacing on purpose) not the specific numbers, and it does not reconcile the separate z-50/z-30 header/sticky-rail scale with the 400-700 overlay scale, a real inconsistency this note surfaces rather than resolves (the existing sticky-header entry at LOCKFILE:825-831 already flags this same unreconciled second scale).
MECHANIC: this is sparse enumeration (CONV), a standard software convention for exactly this problem, documented explicitly in Bootstrap's own z-index utility scale (which uses the identical shape: uniform 10-point gaps across all seven of its tiers, 1000 through 1070, stated in Bootstrap's own docs as headroom for custom values). Solen's scale extends the same idea with variable gap sizes: a tight 10-point gap for a background/foreground pair that will never need an insertion between them, and a wide 90 to 100-point gap between semantically distinct overlay types (sheet, modal, toast, tooltip) where a future layer type plausibly could slot in between. This upgrades the z-index entry from "CONV, chosen for insertion headroom, not derived" (its current section-14 language) to a named, citable instance of a recognized pattern; it is still not a formula that outputs 10 or 90 specifically.
SOURCE: Bootstrap z-index utility docs (CONV), getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/utilities/z-index; LOCKFILE:494-497; LOCKFILE:825-831 (the unreconciled second scale, already flagged); RATIONALE.md section 18.
draft.taste_lab_probe: Not applicable in the generative-prior sense (this stream is canon-deepen, not generative-gap), but the gap register could log a low-priority open question for a future round: whether the header/sticky-rail z-30/z-50 scale should be folded into the 400-700 scale (e.g. renamed to a 4-digit-consistent value) is a real unreconciled seam worth a owner yes/no, not a taste probe.

verified.title: Elevation / shadow rgba + z-index scale grounding

claim_verdicts.claim: Material Design elevation shadow system layers a key shadow over an ambient shadow with named opacity constants key-umbra 0.20, key-penumbra 0.14, ambient 0.12, shifting as dp increases.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed live: m1.material.io/resources/shadows.html is a real archived Material Design 1 page and multiple independent sources (codepen implementations, mdui.org mirror) reproduce the same 0.20/0.14/0.12 opacity triad. Correctly tiered CONV, a named documented system, not an empirical study.

claim_verdicts.claim: The penumbra of a cast shadow widens as the distance between object and surface grows, for a fixed-size light source, as a general fact of shadow-formation optics.
claim_verdicts.note: Standard geometric optics, matches the Wikipedia umbra/penumbra/antumbra overview the draft cites. No inflation, correctly tiered T1 (general physical fact, not a specific study).

claim_verdicts.claim: Sparse enumeration (deliberate numeric gaps) is a named engineering convention documented in Bootstrap's z-index utility docs, which use uniform 10-point gaps across seven tiers from 1000 through 1070, for exactly the insertion-headroom reason.
claim_verdicts.note: REFUTED on two specifics, not the underlying claim. (1) Wrong URL/section: getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/utilities/z-index documents only the LOW single-digit z-n1..z-3 utility classes; the 1000+ overlay scale lives on a different page, getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/layout/z-index/. (2) Wrong numbers: live-checked Bootstrap 5.3 values are dropdown 1000, sticky 1020, fixed 1030, offcanvas-backdrop 1040, offcanvas 1045, modal-backdrop 1050, modal 1055, popover 1070, tooltip 1080, toast 1090, i.e. NOT uniform 10-point gaps (they run 20/10/10/5/5/5/15/10/10) and the scale does not stop at 1070, it runs to 1090 across ten tiers, not seven. The draft's numbers_used array even lists a fabricated value, 1010, which does not exist anywhere in Bootstrap's real scale, a tell that the specific sequence was invented rather than read off the source. The underlying convention (sparse enumeration for insertion headroom) is real and Bootstrap DOES use it, and its real numbers are actually a slightly better match for Solen's ask than the fabricated ones: Bootstrap's own tightest gaps (5, between each backdrop and its own foreground element, offcanvas-backdrop/offcanvas and modal-backdrop/modal) are precisely the same shape as Solen's tight scrim/sheet pairing the draft wanted to justify. Correction downgrades the citation from a precise-numbers claim to a shape-only precedent.

verified.residual_risks: The z-index paragraph's BOUNDARY line correctly surfaces but does not resolve a real tension: Solen runs two disconnected z-index scales (the 400-700 overlay scale in LOCKFILE:494-497 and a separate z-30/z-50 header/sticky-rail scale flagged at LOCKFILE:825-831). This addition does not touch either frozen value, per instructions, but the owner should get a QUESTIONS.md candidate: should the two scales eventually be unified onto one numbering convention, given a future overlay could plausibly need to stack relative to both a modal AND a sticky header. Separately, the Material Design source (m1.material.io) is Google's now-superseded v1 Material Design site, current Material 3 uses a different elevation model (tonal surfaces more than layered shadows); the addition cites m1 explicitly and correctly scopes it as the historical two-shadow convention Solen's stack resembles, not current Material 3 guidance, so no correction needed there but worth knowing if a future pass tries to extend the citation to Material 3.
